newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGRI-LA SHARES FALL AFTER RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: SHANGRI-LA SHARES FALL AFTER RESULTS.

text.p: Shares of Shangri-La Asia Ltd fell on Thursday after the company reported a decline in interim net profit and announced an acquisition which investors feared would dilute earnings, brokers said.
The stock fell HK$0.40 to HK$8.40 in early trade.
Shangri-La Asia posted a 6.3 percent fall in interim net profit to HK$470.95 million for the six months to June 30.
"We were expecting two to three percent growth in the first half," said Philip Chan, an analyst at Yamaichi International.
"We will revise down our full-year estimates."

Shangri-La Asia also said on Wednesday it had agreed to buy 100 percent of SLIM International Ltd from its parent the Kuok Group for HK$1.2 billion to be paid through the issue of 135.9 million new shares at HK$8.83 each.
"Even though the issue price of the new shares was above its Wednesday close, the fear of dilution triggered selling," said Edwin Cheung, sales manager at Taiwan Securities.
Chan said while the acquisition was a good move, Shangri-La Asia shares seemed expensive at current levels.
